summary: Introduces the Scalable Address Resolution Protocol, an architecture that uses proxy gateways to help large data centers scale. The proxies reduce the size of switch forwarding tables and the impact of ARP and Neighbor Discovery traffic. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: In a huge building, a front desk answers where is room X, so no one needs to shout down the hallways.

questions: reduce arp traffic in large data centers
subtitle: Reduce address table explosion in large data centers using proxy gateways.

tldr.problem: Large data centers with virtual machines spread across multiple access domains face two critical scaling problems: switches' MAC address tables explode in size when exposed to thousands of VMs across many VLANs, and ARP/Neighbor Discovery traffic overwhelms the gateways that connect subnets.
tldr.mechanism: SARP uses proxy gateways at domain boundaries that intercept and rewrite ARP and ND messages, hiding VM MAC addresses from the interconnecting network and reducing forwarding table sizes to just the proxy addresses.
tldr.outcome: Switches only learn proxy MAC addresses, not individual VM addresses, keeping forwarding tables manageable regardless of VM count. ARP/ND traffic is significantly reduced, protecting gateway CPUs from being overwhelmed.

facts.label: Targets
facts.value: Large data centers with VM mobility

today: RFC 7586 is an Experimental RFC introducing the Scalable Address Resolution Protocol for data center networks. It has not been obsoleted. The IESG notes that the problems SARP addresses can also be solved through combinations of existing techniques such as Layer 2 VPN, proxy ARP, and proxy Neighbor Discovery.

sections.title: The Large Data Center Scaling Problem
sections.content:
Traditional data centers kept subnets physically isolated in small groups of servers. Modern data centers stretch a single subnet across many physical locations and racks to support virtual machine (VM) mobility. When a subnet spans multiple access domains and each domain hosts VMs from many different subnets, intermediate switches are exposed to the MAC addresses of all VMs in all enabled VLANs.

For example, an access switch with 40 physical servers, each hosting 100 VMs, has 4,000 attached MAC addresses. If those VMs belong to 4,000 different VLANs, and each VLAN has 200 hosts globally, the switch's MAC address table (FDB) could hold 800,000 entries—far beyond the capacity of typical switching hardware.

In parallel, the L2/L3 boundary gateways that connect access networks to the core are hit with a storm of ARP and Neighbor Discovery (ND) requests from thousands of VMs. When VMs on different subnets attached to the same gateway do not communicate frequently, the gateway processes ARP/ND twice: once from the source VM and once for the destination. At large scale, this CPU load can exhaust gateway resources and cause frame drops.
sections.eli5: When computers get spread out over a huge building and need to talk to each other, they all ask the main switch where to find each other. If there are thousands of computers, the switch's brain explodes trying to remember where everyone is and answering all the questions.

sections.title: SARP Architecture and Proxy Gateways
sections.content:
SARP addresses these problems by placing proxy gateways at the boundaries where local Layer 2 networks connect to interconnecting networks. The key insight is that all VMs under one access domain are represented by the MAC address of their local proxy, not by individual VM MAC addresses.

When host A on the west site wants to reach host B on the same subnet but at the east site, A looks up B's address using ARP or ND. Instead of learning B's actual MAC address, A learns the MAC address of the SARP proxy at the east site. The proxy gateways then rewrite MAC addresses as packets pass through, hiding individual VM addresses from the interconnecting network and from remote sites.

SARP proxies can be implemented at various points in the data center architecture: at the hypervisor on a server, at the top-of-rack switch, at an aggregation switch, or at the data center edge. The architecture works with flat Layer 2 domains and integrates cleanly with overlay networks like VXLAN and NVGRE that provide Layer 2 virtualization across data centers.
sections.eli5: Instead of everyone knowing where everyone else is, they just know the phone number of a secretary at each location. When you want to call room X at another site, you call the secretary there and she connects you.

sections.title: How SARP Operates
sections.content:
In SARP, the control plane (ARP and ND) and the data plane (actual packet transmission) behave differently. When a source VM sends an ARP request for a destination VM on a different site, the local SARP proxy intercepts it and, if it does not already know the destination IP-to-MAC mapping, forwards the request to other sites while replacing the source MAC address with its own. This ensures switches in the interconnecting network see only proxy MAC addresses, not VM addresses.

When the destination VM replies, the remote SARP proxy receives the response and replaces the destination MAC address with its own MAC address before forwarding it back. The source VM thus learns "the MAC address I should use for the destination is the remote SARP proxy's MAC."

For the data plane, when host A sends an actual packet to host B, the packet carries A's IP and the proxy MAC learned from ARP. The local SARP proxy rewrites the source MAC to its own address before forwarding to the interconnecting network. The remote SARP proxy rewrites the destination MAC back to B's actual address before delivering locally.

SARP proxies maintain ARP/ND caches that can be queried for remote VM addresses, significantly reducing the volume of ARP/ND traffic crossing the interconnecting network.
sections.eli5: When you ask where someone is, the secretary rewrites the question so the other secretary knows which office to answer for. When the answer comes back, they rewrite it again so you think the other secretary is the person you're looking for.

sections.title: Virtual Machine Migration
sections.content:
When a VM migrates from one site to another while keeping its IP and MAC addresses, ARP/ND caches at other sites must be updated. If a Gratuitous ARP (IPv4) or Unsolicited Neighbor Advertisement (UNA) message is sent by the destination after the VM arrives, all sites update their ARP caches to point the VM's IP address to the new site's SARP proxy MAC.

During the transition, before ARP caches age out, VMs at the origin site may still send packets with the old proxy MAC. These packets arrive at the old proxy, which must detect the mismatch and redirect them to the new location or the packets will be dropped. This transient condition can be resolved by sending a Gratuitous ARP/UNA message immediately after migration, using a shorter ARP cache aging timer, or by having the old proxy redirect unknown MAC destinations.

VM migration within a single site requires no SARP-specific behavior; Layer 2 mechanisms handle it as usual.
sections.eli5: When someone moves to a different office, everyone else needs to hear "hey, this person is now at the East office" so they know where to find them. Until everyone gets that update, some messages might get sent to the old office.

sections.title: Deployment and Comparison with Alternatives
sections.content:
SARP can be deployed in different configurations depending on data center topology. The RFC focuses on flat Layer 2 domains where SARP proxies sit at the edge, connecting the data center to the transport network. SARP can also be placed at the aggregation layer or implemented by hypervisors on servers themselves.

Existing IETF solutions address related problems but require hosts in one subnet to be located together under one access domain. SARP is designed for the case where hosts in one subnet are spread across multiple access domains and each access domain contains hosts from many different subnets. Layer 2 VPN (RFC 4664), proxy ARP (RFC 925), and proxy ND (RFC 4389) work well in traditional architectures but do not prevent FDB table explosion when VM mobility is introduced.

SARP is backward compatible with these solutions and can be deployed incrementally. For high availability, multiple SARP proxies can serve a single site, with each proxy handling a subset of VLANs as master and the others as backup. A keepalive mechanism detects failures and promotes a backup proxy to master.
sections.eli5: You can put secretaries in different places depending on how your building is arranged. This approach works especially well for modern buildings where people move around a lot, unlike older solutions that assumed people stayed in the same place.
